# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 27 (Bu-Vb Np27)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np27
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 27
**Title (English, from literature):** Bribing weavers
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāpesakāra Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 27) is a vinaya rule in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* concerning the procurement of robe-cloth. The rule addresses situations where a lay devotee arranges for weavers to produce cloth intended for a monastic: if the monk approaches the weavers without prior invitation and makes demands or offers incentives to alter the weave, he incurs an offense requiring the forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) of the finished robe-cloth and confession (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

This training rule forms an integral part of Buddhist monastic legal codes. In the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to the twenty-seventh rule of the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and parallels Nissaggiya Pācittiya 28 of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, as well as their respective treatments in the *Parivāra*. Curated parallels exist widely across Buddhist schools and canonical languages, appearing in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsāṃghika traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions (frequently numbered as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 24, 12, or 27).
